Title: Independent modules
Decision: Each module owns state and is integrated through ASET Protocol; no shared internal tables or direct state mutation.

Title: Monade ownership
Decision: Monade owns Task/Plan/Transition lifecycles only.
Rationale: Prevents God object and protects module semantics.

Title: Core independence
Decision: Core has no dependency on Memory, Master, Monade or Gateway.
Rationale: Keeps normative decision auditable and reusable.

Title: Memory four-model lifecycle
Decision: Separate EventIngestion, CandidateDecision, MemoryItem lifecycle and EpistemicStatus.

Title: Verifier authority
Decision: Verifier issues VerificationReceipt; Memory applies it and cannot self-verify.

Title: Decision versus Permit
Decision: Core verdict ALLOW is a DecisionRecord; Permit is a separate bounded capability artifact.

Title: Three transactional boundaries
Decision: Use three local transactions around intent, observation and outcome.
Rationale: External effects cannot be enclosed in one database transaction.

Title: Compensation model
Decision: Compensation is a new independently authorized transition and only follows evidence of effect footprint.

Title: Master evidence levels
Decision: DESCRIPTIVE, ASSOCIATIONAL, MATCHED_OBSERVATIONAL, QUASI_EXPERIMENTAL, CONTROLLED_EXPERIMENTAL.

Title: Canonical protocol profile
Decision: Canonical semantic schema and canonical JSON profile are mandatory; binary profiles are optional.
Rationale: Keeps MVP small and semantics stable.

Title: Provider state
Decision: Provider conversations are disposable caches, never canonical memory.

Title: Context read authorization
Decision: Monade obtains a Core decision/permit before restricted Memory retrieval in managed/strict profiles.

Title: Receipts and integrity
Decision: All cross-module material decisions produce versioned digest-bearing receipts; strict profile requires signatures.

Title: Risk tiers and human gates
Decision: R0-R4 determine human control and nondelegable action classes.

Title: PostgreSQL role
Decision: PostgreSQL is preferred reference platform but not architecture definition.

Title: Outbox dispatch
Decision: External effects are dispatched only from durable intent/outbox after commit.

Title: Memory indexes
Decision: Graph/vector/hierarchy/holographic forms are derived indexes.

Title: Task terminal states
Decision: Only COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, INVALID, SUPERSEDED and EXHAUSTED are terminal; waits/suspension are nonterminal.

Title: Conformance profiles
Decision: Define Core-only, Contextual, Advisory, Managed and Strict profiles.

Title: Quality taxonomy
Decision: ISO/IEC 25010:2023 is primary quality map; FURPS+ is secondary reporting view.

Title: Requirements hierarchy
Decision: Stakeholder needs derive system requirements; system requirements derive module/interface/data requirements.

Title: Freeze governance
Decision: Freeze requires owner approval record, hashes, clean-room build and zero open Critical/High findings.

Title: Privacy and legal controls
Decision: Legal basis, purpose, jurisdiction, retention, hold and data-subject rights are first-class controls.

Title: Observability privacy
Decision: Telemetry contains IDs/digests by default; content requires explicit policy.

Title: Tool classification
Decision: Tools are Pure, Read, Mutating or Critical; execution path depends on class.

Title: Unknown handling
Decision: UNKNOWN never implies allow or success; handling is policy-driven evidence request, human escalation or fail-closed.

Title: Reference code status
Decision: Existing code is non-normative; compatibility is established only by conformance tests.

Title: Open-source boundary
Decision: Specification, protocol, conformance suite and reference data plane are open; commercial value is support, managed control plane, certifications and process packs.

Title: Master owns planning and expected change
Decision: ASET Master includes planning, criticism and replanning and is the sole semantic owner and signer of ExpectedChangePatch.
Rationale: Removes the ownerless Planner and prevents Monade or Core from inventing desired state.

Title: Core is sole Permit issuer
Decision: ASET Core is the only component allowed to create an authority-bearing Permit. Other signatures are evidence, provenance or approval only.
Rationale: Eliminates dual authority and implicit permissions.

Title: Binary Core resolution and default deny
Decision: CoreResolution is PERMITTED or PROHIBITED. No Permit is issued unless explicit issuance conditions are satisfied; no resolution or technical failure is fail-closed.

Title: One document one gate one crossing
Decision: A Permit is bound to one exact document digest, dependency context set, gate instance, crossing ID, actor/execution and one immediate crossing.
Rationale: Implements least authority and prevents replay or scope transfer.

Title: Immutable signed composite context
Decision: Operational Context is a Merkle-rooted manifest of immutable components signed by semantic owners. Signatures prove origin and integrity, not truth or authority.
Rationale: Supports auditability, scoped concurrency and independent ownership.

Title: Gate is the linearization point
Decision: A gate atomically validates the source dependency set and Permit, forms a deterministic patch set, creates new context components/root, updates scoped HEADs, consumes Permit and emits a crossing receipt.
Rationale: Removes TOCTOU and ambiguous distributed state.

Title: Expectation and execution are separately authorized
Decision: Expectation admission and external execution use different documents, gates and incompatible one-shot Permits. ExpectationPermit never authorizes an external effect.
Rationale: Prevents an authorized goal from becoming broad tool authority.

Title: Two-component Monade
Decision: ASET Monade contains semantically independent Execution and Acceptance components. Execution organizes work; Acceptance independently verifies and accepts it.

Title: Deterministic prompt compilation
Decision: Prompt Compiler is a deterministic Monade Execution subsystem that compiles a context projection into PromptManifest; Model Gateway only renders provider format.
Rationale: Makes model input reproducible and prevents provider state becoming canonical.

Title: Expected observed verified accepted are distinct
Decision: EXPECTED, OBSERVED, VERIFIED/REJECTED/PARTIAL/UNKNOWN and TaskAcceptance are separate typed claims and transitions.
Rationale: Prevents self-confirming context and false completion.

Title: Memory and operational Context are distinct
Decision: ASET Memory owns long-term knowledge; operational Context is a signed task-scoped working projection that can reference Memory receipts.
Rationale: Avoids invalidating execution on unrelated memory changes.

Title: Scoped context dependencies
Decision: Permits declare exact read_set/write_set component digests. Only dependency changes invalidate a Permit; cross-component writes are all-or-nothing.
Rationale: Enables parallelism without a single global HEAD.

Title: External effect boundary
Decision: Dispatch gate commits ExecutionIntent and OutboxCommand in ASET context; it does not claim atomic or exactly-once external effect. Connectors require idempotency and reconciliation.
Rationale: Makes distributed guarantees honest and implementable.

Title: Machine-readable model is normative
Decision: The JSON/YAML system model, system specification and JSON Schemas are normative package sources. Generated documents and registries must conform to them.
Rationale: Prevents prose/model drift and enables automated audit.

Title: Acceptance owns outcome classification
Decision: Monade Acceptance owns VerificationVerdict, AcceptanceDecision, operational/normative outcome and TaskAcceptance; Core owns authority only.
Rationale: Separates power from truth and completion.

Title: Closed-world schema profile
Decision: All normative JSON artifacts reject unknown properties and validate date-time formats; OneShotPermit is a closed union of all gate-specific Permit schemas.
Rationale: Prevents schema confusion and silent authority extension.

Title: Complete gate contract triads
Decision: Every gate owns a distinct Submission, Permit and append-only Patch schema plus a machine-readable TransitionSpec.
Rationale: Makes gate semantics implementable and mutation-testable.

Title: Composite context cryptographic profile
Decision: ASET-MERKLE-1 fixes component leaf fields, canonical ordering, owner mapping and Merkle construction; Ed25519-SHA256-v1 and ASET-JCS-1 have reproducible vectors.
Rationale: Eliminates ambiguity in context roots and signatures.

Title: Deterministic prompt contract
Decision: PromptManifest binds source dependencies, projection/compiler/model/tokenizer profiles, token budget, selection policy, canonical messages and prompt bytes digest.
Rationale: Makes prompt compilation reproducible and auditable.

Title: Release finalization order
Decision: Generated artifacts are rebuilt first; conformance and semantic document hashes are checked; MANIFEST and SHA256SUMS are produced last.
Rationale: Prevents manifest invalidation by post-manifest document generation.
